title: Projected logical ensembles in surface codes via the random-matrix theory of quantum dots
authors: Mircea Bejan, Jan Behrends, Max McGinley, Benjamin Béri
abstract: Measurements underpin active quantum error correction (QEC) and have been recognized as a source of novel measurement-induced many-body phenomena. Here, we study the statistical properties of post-measurement logical states arising in QEC on topological codes subject to deterministic transversal unitary gates. Upon syndrome extraction followed by maximum-likelihood decoding, a Born-weighted ensemble arises which we dub the "projected logical ensemble" (PLE). Focusing on surface codes subject to uniform single-qubit Pauli-$X$ rotations, we characterize the measurement-induced randomness of the PLE. To this end, we show that for a code with a single logical qubit, the PLE is isomorphic to an ensemble of scattering matrices describing mesoscopic quantum dots obtained from a 2D Majorana network model with suitable boundary conditions. We uncover regimes where these quantum dots are chaotic such that their scattering matrices are well-described by random matrix theory. In these regimes, the PLE approaches a universal ensemble that is maximally random up to symmetry and decoder-induced constraints. The symmetry constraints, set by stabilizer and logical operator weights, realize Altland-Zirnbauer classes D or DIII, which we both illustrate. Our results establish a fundamental connection between emergent universality concepts in mesoscopic physics, quantum many-body systems, and QEC.
summary: This work analyzes the randomness induced in quantum error correction codes (like the surface code) after syndrome measurements. It establishes that this resulting ensemble of logical states is mathematically equivalent to the scattering matrix statistics of a quantum dot. This connection allows researchers to use established tools from random matrix theory and mesoscopic physics to predict fundamental properties of fault-tolerant quantum computation.
main_problem: The study characterizes the statistical properties of post-measurement logical states (the Projected Logical Ensemble, PLE) arising in Quantum Error Correction (QEC) on topological codes.
main_result: The PLE is shown to be isomorphic to the scattering matrix ensemble of a quantum dot, establishing a fundamental link between QEC universality and mesoscopic physics.
method: The analysis maps the syndrome extraction process onto calculating the scattering matrix ($S$) of an effective quantum dot network derived from the surface code structure.
model_or_system: The system uses the Surface Code (SC) on 2D lattices, where measurement back-action generates randomness. This is mathematically mapped to a mesoscopic quantum dot whose transport properties are governed by Random Matrix Theory (RMT).
key_observables: Projected Logical Ensemble (PLE), scattering matrices ($S$), bulk conductivity ($g$), and the Wasserstein-1 distance ($W_1$) used for comparison.
important_parameters: The coherent rotation angle ($\phi$) determines the regime, with a critical threshold $\phi_{th}$ separating insulating/coherent regimes from metallic/chaotic ones.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes maximum-likelihood decoding and relies on establishing an isomorphism between the quantum circuit evolution and the scattering matrix of the associated quantum dot.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the SC geometry, its mapping to a network model with $S$-matrices, and plots show the dependence of bulk conductivity ($g$) and logical error rate ($P_L$) on the rotation angle $\phi$, identifying critical thresholds.
paper_structure: The paper develops by first defining the PLE via syndrome measurement (Chunk 1), establishing the isomorphism to quantum dot scattering matrices (Chunks 2 & 4), analyzing constraints using tensor networks and symmetry classes (Chunks 3, 5), and finally quantifying the transition between regimes using RMT diagnostics like conductance scaling (Chunks 6 & 7).
why_interesting: It provides a powerful physical realization of abstract concepts in QEC by connecting them directly to well-understood physics models from condensed matter theory, specifically mesoscopic transport phenomena.

FIG. 6. Bulk conductivity g for the network model of the honeycomb surface code under coherent rotations. The system length and width are 21 ≤L = M ≤91 with data averaged over 105 to 106 syndrome realizations. Error bars (SE) are imperceptible. g scales with a ϕ-dependent length ℓ(ϕ). For the insulator ϕ < ϕth, g(L/ℓ(ϕ)) decreases with L, with ϕth = (0.089 ± 0.002)π. For the metal ϕ > ϕth, g increases and, for large L, is consistent with the scaling g ∝(2π)−1 ln[L/ℓ(ϕ)] of a nonlinear sigma model in class DIII in the replica limit N →1 (dashed black line), see also [77, 78].

FIG. 5. Logical error rate PL vs coherent error angle ϕ for the honeycomb surface code with length L. PL decays with L below the error threshold ϕth (vertical dashed red line). The inset shows data closer to the QEC transition. For ϕ > ϕth, PL initially increases with L, after which it becomes weakly dependent on L for the accessible system sizes. The horizontal dotted black line shows the minimum average infidelity for post-QEC states Haar-distributed over a Bloch hemisphere. Error bars show the standard error of the mean (SE).
